p: ye the LORD: The prophet exhorts the people to praise God for his past benefits, that by this their minds may be strengthened against all present troubles and despair.
keep judgment: He shows that it is not enough to praise God with the mouth, unless the whole heart agrees to it, and all our life framed after it.
favour that thou bearest unto thy: Let the good will that you bear to your people extend to me, that by it I may be received into your number.
sinned with our fathers: By earnest confession of their sins and of their father's, they show that they hoped that God according to his promise would pity them.
saved them for his name's sake: The inestimable goodness of God appears in this, that he would rather change the order of nature than have his people not be delivered, even though they were wicked.
believed they his words: The wonderful words of God caused them to believe for a time, and to praise him.
counsel: The would prevent his wisdom and providence.
leanness into their soul: The abundance that God gave them did not profit, but made them pine away, because God cursed it.
swallowed up Dathan: By the greatness of the punishment the heinousness of the offence may be considered: for they who rise against God's ministers rebel against him.
glory into the similitude of an: He shows that all idolaters renounce God to be their glory when instead of him, they worship any creature much more wood, stone, metal or calves.
not Moses his chosen stood before: If Moses, by his intercession, had not obtained God's favour against their rebellion.
the pleasant land: That is Canaan, which acted as a promise of the heavenly inheritance to come, though it was only worth a penny in comparison to the value of the inheritance itself.
he lifted up his hand against: That is, he swore. Sometimes also it means to punish.
Baalpeor: Which was the idol of the Moabites.
dead: Sacrifices offered to the dead idols.
provoked him to anger with their: Signifying that whatever man invents of himself to serve God by, is detestable and provokes his anger.
Phinehas: When all others neglected God's glory, he in his zeal killed the adulterers and prevented God's wrath.
counted unto him for righteousness unto: This act declared his living faith, and for his faith's sake was accepted.

Moses for their sakes: If so notable a prophet of God does not escape punishment, though others provoked him to sin, how much more will they be subject to God's judgment, who cause God's children to sin?
sons and their daughters unto devils: He shows how monstrous a thing idolatry is, which can win us to things abhorring to nature, while God's word cannot obtain small things.
a whoring with their own inventions: Then true chastity is to cleave wholly and only to God.
times did he deliver them: The prophet shows that neither by menace nor promise we can come to God, unless we are altogether newly reformed, and his mercy covers and hides our malice.
repented according to the multitude of: Not that God is changeable in himself, but that then he seems to us to repent when he alters his punishment, and forgives us.
gather us from among the heathen: Gather your Church which is dispersed, and give us constancy under the cross, that with one consent we may all praise you.
